source.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura Coupling in t-Amyl Alcohol for the Preparation of 5-(Furan-3-yl)pyrimidine

reaction.notes: Coupling of heterocyclic substrates with aryl boronic acids, NiCl2(PCy3)2-catalyzed Suzuki–Miyaura coupling of 5-bromopyrimidine with 3-furanylboronic acid in tert-amyl alcohol under nitrogen.
reaction.tags: nickel; Suzuki–Miyaura; t-amyl alcohol; K3PO4; low-loading (0.5 mol %)

quench: Add deionized water (100 mL) and diethyl ether (200 mL); stir 15 min.
workup: Pour into separatory funnel; rinse flask with H2O (100 mL) and Et2O (100 mL).
Separate layers; wash organic layer with 1.0 M NaOH (2 × 200 mL) and saturated NaCl (200 mL).
Dry over Na2SO4 (100 g, 15 min); filter through Celite (30 g); rinse with Et2O (100 mL).
Concentrate by rotary evaporation (275 mmHg, 30 °C; then 30 mmHg, 50 °C).

purification.eluent: Hexanes (200 mL) hot solution at 80 °C; cool to rt then −20 °C (12 h); filter and wash with cold hexane (100 mL). Second recrystallization from mother liquor.

notes: Isolated total: 7.60 g (83%) of 5-(furan-3-yl)pyrimidine as light tan crystals.
Color changes: reddish heterogeneous at 23 °C → brown at 120 °C; brown/greenish upon completion.

original_procedure: A flame-dried 1 L flask charged with K3PO4 (anhydrous) is cooled under nitrogen, then 5-bromopyrimidine, 3-furanylboronic acid, and NiCl2(PCy3)2 are added. After equiping a reflux condenser and performing three N2 evacuate/backfill cycles, t-AmOH (210 mL) is cannula-added under argon to give a reddish mixture. The reaction is stirred at 23 °C for 1 h under positive N2 pressure, then heated at 120 °C for 1 h. The mixture is worked up by dilution with water and diethyl ether, aqueous base and brine washes, drying (Na2SO4), filtration through Celite, and concentration. The residue is recrystallized from hot hexanes (80 °C), cooled to −20 °C to give product as light tan crystals; a second recrystallization of the mother liquor provides additional product. [Paraphrased from first step.]
